title: The Moon Arrives Fashionably Early
skyStory: The moon pours itself into Pisces at ninety-eight percent full, a little early for its own party and dripping with dreamy light. Neptune, ruler of Pisces, has filled the sky with fog machines. Two fish swim circles around the moon like excited puppies. The tides are enormous tonight and incredibly smug about it. Mars says it is fine with the fog. Mars is not fine with the fog.

reading: Pisces makes everything soft around the edges, including your schedule. Things you thought were firm will drift. Let them. A meeting moves. A plan blurs. Underneath, something clearer is rising, like a seal surfacing in the bay. Watch for it around 3 pm.

Tonight, a big bright moon will hang over the treetops near the cabin, almost full, glowing through a light haze. Step outside for one minute and look at it. Not a photo, just a look. The Fire Tiger gets very quiet when it remembers how big the sky is. That quiet is a kind of fuel. Store some for later.
joel.mission: Stand outside for one full minute tonight and look at the moon without taking a single picture.
joel.omen: Fog rolling in faster than expected. A plan will change in a way that turns out better.

reading: Your dreams last night or tonight may be extremely odd and very vivid: talking otters, a library made of seaweed, a staircase that leads into a teacup. Your Life Path 11 should take notes. One detail in the dream is a clue to something real.

During the day, people will be a little foggy and forgetful, and you will be the clear one, the lighthouse on the point. Somebody will thank you for remembering a detail they lost. The [[Queen of Cups]] raises a jewelled goblet in your direction, which is her way of saying trust the hunch.
nancy.mission: Write down the strangest dream detail you can remember the moment you wake, before brushing your teeth.
nancy.omen: An otter, a seal, or a picture of one. Your intuition is especially sharp; use it today.

together.text: Swap the weirdest dream either of you can remember from this year. Interpret each other's dream in the style of an overly confident professor who has never been wrong. Neptune is grading. Neptune awards points for creativity, not accuracy.

game.intro: The full moon showed up a day early with a casserole. Tell us your arrival style, then guess your partner in crime's.
game.question: Be honest: how do you arrive at a party?
